findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty/null and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. When the event has no destination calendar (null or empty array — common for users with no connected calendar), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError. Previously this line used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so it was safe. Any booking with location `integrations:google:meet` and no destination calendar will now fail during event creation. The check should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback lookup compares externalCalendarId to itself and can never match
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (and the identical pattern in `deleteEvent` at line 317), the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Searching for a calendar whose externalId equals the (falsy) externalCalendarId can never succeed, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, failing the API call. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which resolved to the host's calendar. The intent appears to be matching the destination calendar against the credential in use, similar to what `createEvent` now does with `credentialId`; as written, updates/deletes for bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` will silently break.

findings.title: hangoutLink patch uses undefined calendarId when fallback "primary" was used for insert
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId (selectedCalendar is undefined), the event is created on "primary" but the follow-up patch is issued with `calendarId: undefined`, so the description with the Meet link is never written (and the promise rejection is unhandled). Apply the same `|| "primary"` fallback to the patch call.

findings.title: createEvent always uses the first destination calendar regardless of which host's credential is used
findings.body: `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` destructures `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and posts to `/me/calendars/{firstCalendar.externalId}/events`. With this PR, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent` once per host credential for collective events, but the service signature was not updated to accept the credentialId/externalId being processed (unlike Google, which received a `credentialId` parameter and picks the matching calendar). For a collective booking, host B's Office365 credential will try to create the event in host A's calendar (whose externalId is meaningless to host B's account), so the call fails or creates the event in the wrong place. The same problem exists in `LarkCalendarService` and `BaseCalendarService` (caldav), which also only ever look at `destinationCalendar[0]`. The per-credential calendar must be selected the same way Google's implementation does.

findings.title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: The new code sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and later does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If the organizer has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, the optional-chained push is a no-op and the hosts' calendars are silently discarded — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix (hosts not getting invited). The collective branch should initialize the array, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: One unresolvable reference aborts updates for all remaining calendar references
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, if a reference has a `credentialId` that is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor found in the DB (deleted credential, or a credential belonging to a collective host that no longer exists), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still pushed into `result`. `updateEvent` calls `getCalendar(undefined)`, which throws; the outer try/catch then swallows everything and returns failure results for all references — so a single stale reference prevents updating every other host's calendar event on reschedule. The loop should skip references whose credential cannot be resolved (with a logged warning) instead of pushing the update.

findings.title: Recurring-event deletes now run once per calendar reference, causing duplicated delete calls
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch (delete all remaining bookings' events across all the user's calendar credentials) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a collective booking with two calendar references, the block that iterates over every user credential and every updated booking is executed once per reference, so each event is deleted N times (and `apiDeletes` collects duplicates). Besides wasted API calls, some providers error on deleting an already-deleted event. Additionally, the inner loop still only deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)` — the first calendar reference per booking — so extra hosts' references are never removed. The recurring-delete block should run once outside the per-reference loop, and should iterate over all calendar references of each updated booking.

findings.title: Unrelated logic inversion in organization slug persistence
findings.body: This PR about destinationCalendar arrays also changes organization creation: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting when the org slug is stored on the team record. This is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose, untested, and changes which deployments persist `slug` vs `requestedSlug` — if unintentional it will break org subdomain resolution; if intentional it belongs in its own PR with justification.

findings.title: No tests cover the new multi-host destinationCalendar behavior
findings.body: The PR checklist explicitly states "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective". This change alters the `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` contract from a single object to an array and rewires create/update/delete paths across Google, Office365, Lark, CalDAV, EventManager, cancellation, rescheduling, and payment webhooks — including subtle per-credential calendar selection and booking reference persistence (`referencesToCreate` now uses `result.externalId`/`result.credentialId`). Given regressions like the empty-array crash in `EventManager.create` and the Office365 first-calendar-only behavior, at minimum unit tests for `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` with multiple hosts and for the no-destination-calendar case should be required before merging.
